memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord also said to Moses, "Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be mine. I am the Lord. To redeem the 273 firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites, collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs. Give the money for the redemption of the additional Israelites to Aaron and his sons." - Num 3:44-48 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There were more firstborn Israelites than there were Levites — 273 more. For those who could not be matched with a Levite substitute, a redemption price was set: five shekels each. The word "redeem" means to buy back, to free by paying a price. These firstborn were "bought back" and released from the obligation of service through a payment.

This is one of the most precious words in the Bible: redemption. It means someone was set free because a price was paid. God built this idea into the life of Israel so that, over centuries, His people would understand what redemption feels like — the joy of being bought back.

Money could redeem the firstborn of Israel. But our redemption from sin required a far greater price. The New Testament tells us we were redeemed "not with perishable things such as silver or gold... but with the precious blood of Christ" (1 Pet 1:18-19). No amount of shekels could buy back a soul; only the blood of the Lamb could do that.

If you belong to Jesus, you have been redeemed — bought back at the greatest cost imaginable. You are not your own; you were bought with a price (1 Cor 6:20).

Live today as one who has been redeemed. You are free, you are His, and the price has been fully paid.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What does it mean to you to be "redeemed" by Christ?
- How does the price paid for you change how you live?
- Are you living as one who has been bought back and set free?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for redeeming me, not with silver or gold, but with Your own precious blood. I am Yours; help me to live as one set free. Amen.
